ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The number of turns of a circular coil is $N=200$, the area of the coil is $S=1\mathrm{m}^{2}$, the resistance of the coil is $r=10\Omega$, and the coil is connected to an external resistor with a resistance of $R=50\Omega$. The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the coil and directed inward. The variation of the magnetic induction over time is shown in Figure B.

1. What is the induced electromotive force generated in the coil?
2. What is the current in the circuit?
3. If the resistance $R$ is a variable resistor, at what value of $R$ is the power consumed by $R$ maximized?
4. What is the maximum power consumed by $R$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is a circular coil, and the area where the coil is located uses multiple “×” marks to indicate that the magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the paper surface and inward. The coil is connected by wires to the external resistor R on the right side. On the right side of the figure is a B-t graph, with the vertical axis labeled B/T and the horizontal axis labeled t/s; the straight line starts rising from B=0.2 T at t=0, and the dashed lines mark that B=0.4 T at t=4 s. Then reason: From the graph, the rate of change of magnetic induction intensity is read as dB/dt=(0.4-0.2)/4=0.05 T/s. The coil plane is perpendicular to the magnetic field, so the magnetic flux of each turn is Φ=BS. The magnitude of the induced electromotive force is obtained from Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction as ε=N S dB/dt=200×1×0.05=10 V. The coil resistance r=10 Ω and the external resistor R=50 Ω are connected in series, and the total resistance is r+R=60 Ω, so the current I=ε/(r+R)=10/60=1/6 A. If R is a variable resistor, the coil can be equivalently regarded as a power source with electromotive force ε=10 V and internal resistance r=10 Ω. The power consumed by the external resistor is P_R=ε²R/(r+R)². According to the maximum power transfer condition, when P_R is maximum, R=r=10 Ω. The maximum power P_max=ε²/(4r)=10²/(4×10)=2.5 W.
